topics.title: Welcome to Magic Git
topics.summary: A native macOS Git client with six sidebar panels, File tabs, and factory-default shortcuts.

sections.text: Magic Git is a native macOS Git client that drives git, gh, and glab on this Mac or on a remote POSIX host over SSH, without cloning the remote repository locally. A connected session has six sidebar panels — Repository, History, Branches, Stashes, Forge, and Worktrees — plus File tabs for more than one repository.
Help versus live shortcuts
This window (Help ▸ Support & Help, ⌘?) is the user guide. It lists factory-default shortcuts. Your remaps are in Keyboard Shortcuts (⌘/) and Settings → Keyboard Mappings.

sections.title: App Sandbox Security
sections.text: Local repository access uses macOS security-scoped bookmarks, so later launches reopen a folder without asking again.

topics.title: Connecting to Repositories
topics.summary: Open a local folder or an SSH host from the Connections Manager and Recent Repositories list.

sections.text: Local Repositories

Use the Connections Manager on the landing screen, or pick a recent repository from Recent Repositories. Add existing repository opens the macOS folder panel. Magic Git stores a security-scoped bookmark so later launches reopen that folder without asking again.
Remote SSH Repositories

Magic Git runs git on the remote host over SSH. Enter the host, username, and port, then load or paste a PEM key or use a password. Keys with passphrases, optional scoped git directories, and host tokens are supported.

sections.title: Automatic Reconnection
sections.text: If SSH drops mid-session, a Connection interrupted overlay retries with an attempt counter and elapsed timer. Stop Retrying pauses auto-reconnect and shows Connection lost (Reconnect or Start Fresh). Cancel fully disconnects and confirms if the session is at risk.

topics.title: Clone and Create Repositories
topics.summary: Provision a new working copy from Connections or the command palette.

sections.text: Clone repository and Create repository live on the Connections Manager toolbar and under app: in the command palette.
Clone

items: Destination — where the new working copy will live.
Source — browse GitHub or GitLab, or paste a URL.
Location — the folder name on the host.
Review — confirm and run. A failed or cancelled clone deletes the partial folder.

sections.text: Create

items: Destination — local Mac or an SSH host.
Source — empty folder or an existing folder.
Remote — create on GitHub or GitLab, a custom URL, or none.
Details — name, initial branch, first commit.
Review — confirm and activate the session.

topics.title: File Tabs and Saved Workspaces
topics.summary: Open several repositories at once, save a set, and confirm before closing dirty work.

sections.text: File tabs are repository sessions, not the six sidebar panels. File ▸ New Tab (⌘T) opens another session. Close Tab is on the File menu only — ⌘W closes a viewer window, not a tab. The strip holds at most 8 tabs and hides when only one is open. Middle-click a tab to close it.

items: An orange dot means uncommitted changes.
A red dot means conflicts.
Saved Workspaces (Connections toolbar or the palette) save, open, delete, or alias a set of tabs.

sections.title: Leaving a session
sections.text: Close tab, Log out, Disconnect, Quit, and Close window confirm when the tree is dirty or a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or revert is in progress.

topics.title: Context Bar, Size, and Menus
topics.summary: How the repository chrome adapts below 720 px and at 1200 px, and what the context bar and menus contain.

sections.text: The workspace is compact below 720 px (navigator or canvas, not both; the sync group collapses; a sidebar toggle sits on the bar), standard from 720 to 1199, and wide at 1200 px and above.
Context bar

The bar always shows the repository identity, watch-health dot, status summary, and one primary action. On SSH it also shows link chips. Leading controls: Back, Forward, then Fetch · Pull · Push · Sync (one emphasized, variants in the overflow). Trailing: Stash, Refresh, Activity, view options. Below 720 px a ⋯ control opens Repository details.
View options

items: Show or hide secondary action labels (off by default).
Show or hide Back, Forward, Sync actions, Stash, Refresh, Activity, View options, Status summary, and Connection status.
Presets Review, Commit, Investigate, and Minimal. Default is Review. Investigate names an inspector slot that is unused — Focus Inspector does nothing.

sections.text: Menus

File, Repository, Branch, Stash, Forge, and Worktree sit in the macOS menu bar with App, Edit, View, Window, and Help. Unavailable items stay visible and dim. View ▸ Focus Navigator, Canvas, Task Dock, and Activity exist and are unbound. Choosing a command from another panel switches there and runs it.

topics.title: File View and Output
topics.summary: The docked file tree (⇧⌘E) and the command Output log (⇧⌘O).

sections.text: File View is View ▸ Show File View (⇧⌘E). It is on by default but hidden until the canvas is at least 1200 px wide unless you Pin file view open. Hide and Collapse all sit on the Files header. There is no Changes | Files switch — the change list stays in the navigator and the tree is this third pane.
Output is a docked command log under the Repository canvas, visible by default. Toggle it with ⇧⌘O. It shows git and SSH invocations, stdout, stderr, and exit codes, including doctor install output.

topics.title: Dashboard, Recovery, and Activity
topics.summary: Session telemetry, reflog snapshots, and the live operations sheet.

sections.text: Dashboard (View ▸ Show Dashboard, ⇧⌘D) is session telemetry — connection, latency, watcher and tool health, forge auth, command counts, and a heatmap of the last 200 commits. It is not the Forge panel.
Recovery (⇧⌘U) is a sheet over HEAD's reflog plus refs/magic-git/snapshots/. Use it for state Undo Git Operation can no longer reach.
Activity is the context-bar bell. It opens a live sheet of running and failed operations, can reveal a command in Output, and can undo the newest undoable record.

topics.title: Settings
topics.summary: Timeouts, identity, sync defaults, appearance, known hosts, and keyboard mappings.

sections.text: Open Settings from Magic Git ▸ Settings… (⌘,), the palette, or this book. Changes apply after Save, except Keyboard Mappings and Forget Host, which save immediately.

items: Command timeouts — network (fetch/pull/push) defaults to 3 minutes; commit defaults to 5 minutes; the floor is 5 seconds.
Committer identity — applied to every commit. Leave blank to use the host git config. Magic Git always records unsigned commits (--no-gpg-sign).
Default sync — Pull / Sync uses Fast-forward only, Rebase, or Merge (default Fast-forward only). Push tags by default is off.
Auto-fetch — Off, or every 5, 10, 15, or 30 minutes. Default is every 5 minutes.
Workspace appearance — Density Compact or Comfortable (default Comfortable), High contrast, Reduce Motion follows macOS.
Known Hosts — Forget a recorded SSH key immediately.
Keyboard Mappings — Customize remaps; they save immediately. The live cheat sheet is ⌘/.
External tools — override binary paths and Scan the host.

topics.title: Repository
topics.summary: Stage, review, resolve conflicts, and commit from the Repository sidebar panel.

sections.text: The Repository panel (⌘1) is a sidebar page, not a File tab. The change list is Conflicts, Staged, Changes, and Untracked, with filter chips, Hide reviewed, and group-by status or directory. Review selected and Review all visible open multi-file review.
Staging and diffs

items: Space toggles staging for the selected file or files.

Line staging works on unified, whitespace-exact diffs with blame off: select lines, then Stage, Unstage, or Discard Selection. Split and ignore-whitespace diffs are read-only. Per-hunk buttons also exist.
Drag unstaged files onto the staging banner to Stage; drag staged files to Unstage.
Conflicts offer Ours, Theirs, and Mark Resolved. A pending banner offers Continue or Abort.

sections.text: Committing

A collapsed Commit… bar sits under the list. ⌘G expands the composer in the task dock — one message field, Accept, and Accept + Push (⇧⌘↩). There is no amend checkbox. Amend Last Commit… is on the Repository menu (unbound). Assistance offers recent subjects, a template, and a policy advisory. Commits are unsigned (--no-gpg-sign).

sections.title: Repository menu only
sections.text: Pull with Rebase, Pull with Merge, Push and Set Upstream, Push Tags, Force Push (no lease), Unstage All, and Abort Pending Operation have no default shortcut. Use the Repository menu or the command palette.

topics.title: History
topics.summary: Commit graph, filters, checkout, rebase, and the History window.

sections.text: The History panel (⌘2) is a sidebar page, not a File tab. It draws a topological commit graph with ref chips and a minimap. The context-bar primary is Refresh.
All Branches versus HEAD

The All Branches control is an icon on the filter bar (tooltip Show all branches), not a labeled toolbar button. It has no keyboard shortcut — ⇧⌘B is Checkout Selected Commit, which asks for confirmation.
Filters and zoom
⌘F focuses the filter. Prefixes include author:, file:, sha:, after:, and before:. Hide merges is a separate chip. Zoom with ⌘=, ⌘-, ⌘0, pinch, or ⌘-scroll.
Commit actions

items: Single commit: Checkout, Branch from…, Branch from… in a new worktree…, Tag…, Cherry-pick, Revert, Interactive rebase, Reset (soft / mixed / hard), Amend last commit (HEAD only), Copy SHA.
Two commits: compare. Several commits: cherry-pick or revert N, copy N SHAs.
Drop a branch onto a commit to merge, rebase, or move that branch here.
Open History in New Window (⇧⌘H) pops a live native History window.

topics.title: Branches
topics.summary: Browse and review local and remote branches, tags, merge, and publish.

sections.text: The Branches panel (⌘3) is a sidebar page, not a File tab. It is master–detail with Browse | Review, pin, hide, and folder grouping. The context-bar primary is Fetch & Prune (no default shortcut). An empty selection shows dashboard stats.
Branch operations

items: ⌘B opens the New branch sheet (name + start-at, default selected ref or HEAD). After Create, choose Here or New worktree.
Double-click or press Enter to check a branch out. You can also check out in a new worktree.
⇧⌘M merges the selected branch into the current branch.
⌘⌫ deletes the selected branch. Unmerged branches confirm.
Rebase the current branch onto another by dragging that branch onto HEAD — there is no Rebase item on the context menu.

sections.title: Review and the Branch menu
sections.text: Review offers compare, Publish, Create Pull or Merge Request, and Open CI. Those four verbs are also on the Branch menu and have no default shortcut. Bulk pin, hide, and delete-if-merged sit on the list.

topics.title: Stashes
topics.summary: Shelve work with include-untracked, then apply, pop, or drop a stash.

sections.text: The Stashes panel (⌘4) is a sidebar page, not a File tab. The list has a filter field. Select a stash to preview its patch.
Creating a stash
Stash Changes (context bar, ⇧⌘S) immediately runs git stash push --include-untracked with no prompt. Untracked files are always included. To set a message, use Stash ▸ Stash with Message….
Applying and removing

items: Apply (⌥⌘A) restores the stash and leaves it on the stack. Pop (⌥⌘P) restores and removes it. Both can use --index.
Drop (⌘⌫) deletes the selected stash after confirmation.
Create branch from stash is on the row menu.
Apply latest, Pop latest, and Clear all are Stash-menu only.

topics.title: Forge
topics.summary: GitHub and GitLab inbox, change requests, issues, and CI traces.

sections.text: The Forge panel (⌘5) is a sidebar page, not a File tab. It talks to GitHub through gh and GitLab through glab. The context-bar primary is New Pull Request or New Merge Request.
Inbox and Browse

Switch Inbox and Browse. Inbox chips filter All / PRs or MRs / CI / Issues. Lists show open items plus a text filter; merged and closed work is not a status chip. Inbox rows can be pinned or snoozed. Browse sections are Issues, PRs or MRs, Labels, Milestones, Releases, and Workflow Runs or Pipelines.
Change requests

items: A merge readiness strip shows blockers. Check out checks out the head branch.
Approve (⌥⌘A), Merge (⇧⌘M), and Re-run or Retry (⌥⌘R) follow the detected host.
Enable or cancel auto-merge from the detail pane. Cancel auto-merge is also on the Forge menu.
Update branch and Rebase onto target sit on the detail More menu.
New Issue is Forge-menu only (no default shortcut).

topics.title: Worktrees
topics.summary: Parallel checkouts in a nested strip — Overview plus Changes, History, Branches, and Stashes.

sections.text: The Worktrees panel (⌘6) is a sidebar page, not a File tab. Opening a worktree adds a checkout tab on the Worktrees strip (Overview | that checkout). That nested strip is not the File-tab switcher. Each checkout tab has Changes, History, Branches, and Stashes. Forge stays on the repository, not the checkout.
Overview
Overview lists every worktree and its state: main, detached, locked, or missing. The Worktree menu (all unbound) offers Add, Open, Lock, Unlock, Move, Repair, Repair All, Prune, and Remove.
Adding a worktree

Add Worktree can create a new branch, use an existing one, or detach. Optional: copy ignored files, run a post-create command. A local add records a security-scoped bookmark. SSH has no sandbox bookmark. A worktree created in the terminal prompts once on first open.

topics.title: File Viewer and Remote Edit
topics.summary: Floating Code and Preview windows, find, wrap, and Open in Default App.

sections.text: File viewer windows are floating overlays, not the docked File View pane. Switch Code and Preview in the title bar. Markdown preview links open in the browser. Escape or ⌘W closes the front viewer.
Open in Default App

On a local repo, Open uses the macOS opener. On SSH, Open in Default App copies the file to a temp path, watches the parent directory, and uploads on save. A conflicting remote change offers overwrite.

topics.title: Diffs, Blame, and File History
topics.summary: Line staging rules, blame, follow-renames history, image diffs, and LFS pointers.

sections.text: The blame gutter is off by default. Show blame on the diff or open the Blame sheet. File history (git log --follow) is on the file tree, not the Changes list.

items: Image diffs show before and after.
Git LFS pointers are named as pointers — run git lfs pull. They are not shown as a binary image.
The file tree can View file, Open, Mark Resolved, act on staged or unstaged halves, Add to .gitignore, or Delete (undoable).

topics.title: Drag and Drop
topics.summary: Stage, stash, cherry-pick, merge, rebase, and create worktrees by dragging.

items: Unstaged files onto the staging banner = Stage; staged files = Unstage.
Files onto Stashes = a path-scoped stash (include-untracked).
A commit onto Repository = cherry-pick (confirm).
A local branch onto Forge = create a pull or merge request.
A commit or branch onto Worktrees = the Add Worktree sheet.
A branch onto a History commit = merge, rebase, or move that branch here.
A commit onto a branch row = cherry-pick onto that branch; a branch onto HEAD = merge or rebase.
Esc cancels a drag.

topics.title: Secondary Windows
topics.summary: Native History, detached Status, and the in-window diff pop-out.

items: The native History window is a singleton (⇧⌘H, View menu, or the palette).
A detached repo window is full Status for that path.
The diff pop-out is an in-window float, not a native window.
While a pop-out is key, native menu key equivalents are stripped so they do not steal from the detached session.

topics.title: Command Palette
topics.summary: Search go, git, forge, and app commands, plus branches, commits, files, stashes, and worktrees.

sections.text: Press ⌘K to open the command palette. Prefix with go:, git:, forge:, app:, branch:, commit:, file:, stash:, or worktree:. file: lists changed paths only, not the whole tree. Open Settings is a command — the palette does not search Settings keys.
Clone, Create, Saved Workspaces, and Manage Connections live under app:. Commit-message and viewer actions are intentionally absent from the palette catalog.

topics.title: Menus and Factory-Default Shortcuts
topics.summary: Every factory-default shortcut, plus menu-only verbs. Remaps live under ⌘/.

sections.text: This topic catalogs every factory-default shortcut. Help ▸ Support & Help is ⌘?. Keyboard Shortcuts (the live cheat sheet of your remaps) is ⌘/. Settings → Keyboard Mappings saves remaps immediately.
Menus
File, Repository, Branch, Stash, Forge, and Worktree hold every toolbar verb. Some chords are shared across scopes (⇧⌘M, ⌥⌘A, ⌘N, ⇧⌘↩, ⌘⌫) — only the active panel's handler runs.
No default shortcut

Use the menu or palette, and bind them in Keyboard Mappings if you want a chord: Toggle Sidebar, Close Tab, Focus Navigator / Canvas / Task Dock / Activity, Pull with Rebase or Merge, Push and Set Upstream, Push Tags, Force Push (no lease), Unstage All, Amend Last Commit… (working tree), Abort Pending, Publish, Create Pull or Merge Request, Open CI, Compare with Base, Stash with Message, Apply/Pop latest, Clear all, every Worktree verb, New Issue, Cancel auto-merge. Focus Inspector exists on the View menu and is unbound; the inspector slot is unused.

topics.title: Local and SSH Sessions
topics.summary: The same UI for a local Mac and a remote host; silent TOFU; Host Key Changed on mismatch.

sections.text: Local repositories use Process.start on this Mac. Remote repositories use the same screens over SSH. Both PEM (with passphrase) and password auth work, as do custom ports.
Host keys

The first time Magic Git sees a host it records the key silently (TOFU). If a known host presents a different fingerprint, a Host Key Changed dialog offers Cancel Connection or Refresh Key and Continue. Settings ▸ Known Hosts can Forget a recorded key.

topics.title: Undo, Redo, and Recovery
topics.summary: ⌘Z undoes the last git operation. Staging is not undoable. Redo is tags only.

sections.text: ⌘Z undoes the last git operation. A toast lasts about five seconds and pauses while you hover. The journal covers commit, amend, reset, checkout, create or delete branch or tag, stash drop/pop/clear/branch, discard, remove files, and hard-reset-shaped merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or revert. Unlike discard, staging is not undoable.

items: ⇧⌘Z redo applies only to atomic tag create or delete.
An empty journal toasts Nothing to undo or Nothing to redo.
Edit ▸ Undo is still text undo in a field.
Recovery (⇧⌘U) reaches reflog and snapshots that ⌘Z cannot.

topics.title: Tool Health
topics.summary: Host probe on a live connection: essential versus feature binaries, Scan, and sideload.

sections.text: Tool health runs on a live connection, not the landing page. Missing essential binaries are errors; missing feature binaries and outdated versions are warnings. Linux hosts are not blamed for a missing fswatch. A banner offers Scan environment; Settings ▸ External tools opens the doctor for one-click install when safe, copy-paste commands, and a sideload drop zone for binaries.

topics.title: Output Log
topics.summary: The docked log of git and SSH invocations, stdout, stderr, and exit codes.

sections.text: Output (⇧⌘O) is the docked command log described in File View and Output. Recovery is a separate sheet — see Dashboard, Recovery, and Activity, and Undo, Redo, and Recovery.
